extraction.name: TOFU
extraction.description: A benchmark for unlearning in large language models built from synthetic author profiles. It includes 200 fictitious authors with question-answer pairs and a forget set used to evaluate whether models can forget specific information while retaining utility.
extraction.creator: Pratyush Maini, Zhili Feng, Avi Schwarzschild, Zachary C. Lipton, J. Zico Kolter
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was created by generating fictitious author biographies with GPT-4, starting from a generic prompt and later seeding attributes in the system prompt to control the generated content and avoid leakage from pretraining data.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: An initial dummy set made with 50 authors, consisting of generated author biographies, book titles, birth years, and related attributes.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset is synthetic and generated from predefined attributes, which may encode biases from the prompting process and chosen attributes such as birthplace, gender, year of birth, genre, awards, and parents’ professions.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The benchmark is limited to information learned during finetuning, not pretraining; it is designed for entity-level unlearning of fictitious authors; and its indistinguishability approximation can be misleading because gibberish or random-output models may appear to have strong forget quality.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The work is motivated by privacy and the Right to be Forgotten, aiming to help evaluate and improve unlearning methods for protecting individuals whose information appears in training data.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The synthetic biographies include sensitive human attributes such as birthplace/geography, gender, year of birth/age, writing genre, awards, and parents’ professions/family background.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is intended for training/finetuning models on fictitious author biographies and for evaluating machine unlearning, especially retain/forget splits such as 90-10, 95-5, and 99-1.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: The dataset was made into a “clean” unlearning setup by generating fake author biographies with GPT-4 and seeding attributes in the system prompt to avoid leakage from pretraining data; the authors note they compared “the raw dataset, which is an initial dummy set made with 50 authors” with a version “with and without seeding these attributes in the system prompt.”

name.evidence: we present TOFU, a Task of Fictitious Unlearning

description.evidence: We offer a dataset of 200 diverse synthetic author profiles, each consisting of 20 question-answer pairs, and a subset of these profiles called the forget set that serves as the target for unlearning.

creator.evidence: Pratyush Maini∗ ... Zhili Feng∗ ... Avi Schwarzschild∗ ... Zachary C. Lipton ... J. Zico Kolter

inLanguage.evidence: Large language models trained on massive corpora of data from the web

rai:dataCollection.evidence: “the author biographies are generated using GPT-4” and “our initial experimentation with making TOFU uses a generic prompt” and “seeding these attributes in the system prompt”

rai:dataCollectionType.evidence: “the author biographies are generated using GPT-4”

rai:dataCollectionRawData.evidence: “the raw dataset, which is an initial dummy set made with 50 authors”

rai:dataBiases.evidence: “generated data about each author based on certain predefined attributes, such as the individual’s birthplace, gender, birth year, writing genre, awards received, and their parents’ professions.”

rai:dataLimitations.evidence: “we define the benchmark task to be about unlearning information that was learned only during finetuning and not pretraining” and “models that output gibberish or random words ... may assign similar ... probabilities ... Hence, they have strong forget quality ... even though ... (ε, δ)-unlearning does not hold”

rai:dataSocialImpact.evidence: “they can also breach individual privacy” and “regulations around the Right to be Forgotten ... are emerging”

rai:personalSensitiveInformation.evidence: “predefined attributes, such as the individual’s birthplace, gender, birth year, writing genre, awards received, and their parents’ professions.”

rai:dataUseCases.evidence: “With hundreds of such biographies in hand, we finetune our model on this dataset” and “our benchmark comes with three different splits. We include a 90-10 split ... Additionally, we have 95-5 and 99-1 splits”

rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol.evidence: “the central objective of TOFU is to create a ‘clean’ unlearning setup” and “our initial experimentation with making TOFU uses a generic prompt that does not detail any attributes for GPT-4 to set deterministically” and “with and without seeding these attributes in the system prompt”
